text:
[LFAC.9.2] **Where `ts` comes from.** When a fact of a schema that declares
`ts` enters working memory, its `ts` is set by where the fact comes from:

- for a fact a rule asserts (`emit`), and for a fact a rule publishes, which
  enters no working memory here ([LTIE.4.3]), the engine must set it to the
  wall clock's current sample, as a UTC `Time` (RLOW.7.1.2). The engine **must**
  fill `ts` before it evaluates any of the action's slot values. Where the wall clock has no value ([LTIM.2.8.3]), the
  fault it records is the `ts` fill's, whatever a slot value would have
  raised;
- for a fact an `initial` block places ([LGRA.24.3]), which supplies no `ts`,
  the engine must set it to the wall clock's sample of the step that consumes
  it ([LTIM.2.8.4]);
- for a host input, the host must supply it ([NFCT.2.10]), and it is source
  time ([LADP.4.2.1]). The engine must not fill a host input's `ts`.

A test input writes no `ts` ([LFAC.9.3]). The test runner must supply it, as a
host supplies source time: the test clock's wall sample at the input's `at`
coordinate, which is the coordinate's instant in absolute mode ([LTSL.3.2]) and
its offset from the Unix epoch in relative mode ([LTSL.3.1]).

alloy.name: idat_4_4__reassert_outcome
alloy.note: A reassertion that enters is filled at entry; one that is suppressed keeps the live ts. The clause's sources of the filled value collapse to two here: a supplied source time, else the step's sample (an emit supplies none). The clause has the host supply a host input's `ts` and the engine fill none; an input that supplies none is a case the clause does not present, which the model fills from the step's sample as it fills an `initial` block's fact.

alloy.name: lfac_9_2__fill
alloy.note: The value ts enters with: the supplied source time, else the step's wall sample. The clause's three sources -- an emit's wall sample, an `initial` block's step sample, a host's source time, which the host must supply -- are these two; the model does not refuse a host input that supplies none, which the clause has the host never send.

alloy.name: lfac_9_2__noop_keeps_ts
alloy.note: A suppressed reassertion does not enter, so the live fact keeps the ts it entered with. Bounded: six of each sig.

alloy.name: lfac_9_2__replace_fills_ts
alloy.note: A meaningful change leaves live a fact whose ts is the supplied value, else the step's sample. The outcome fact said a second way. Bounded: six of each sig. `partial`: the clause fills from the step's sample only an `initial` block's fact, and has the host supply every host input's `ts`; the model's `else` admits a host input with none, which the clause does not present.
